name: San Marino
summary: White over light blue with the coat of arms in the centre: three towers on three peaks of Mount Titano, under a crown, with the motto 'LIBERTAS'. San Marino claims to be the world's oldest surviving republic, founded in 301.
origin: White and light blue have been used since the 18th century. The flag with the coat of arms was officially adopted on 6 April 1862.
The current specifications were set by a 2011 law. The crown on the arms symbolises sovereignty, not monarchy.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The snow on Mount Titano, and peace.

colors.name: Light blue
colors.meaning: The sky over the country, and liberty.

symbols.name: Three towers
symbols.description: Towers with ostrich feathers on three green peaks.
symbols.meaning: The three towers of San Marino, Guaita, Cesta and Montale, on the peaks of Mount Titano.

symbols.name: LIBERTAS
symbols.description: The motto on a ribbon below the shield.
symbols.meaning: Liberty: San Marino's independence over many centuries.

symbols.name: Crown
symbols.description: A closed crown above the shield.

facts: The civil flag has no coat of arms.
San Marino is entirely surrounded by Italy.
Its three towers appear on its euro coins.
clues: White over light blue with a shield of three towers on three peaks.
A tiny republic surrounded by another country claims founding in 301.
